unit: V8 Inspector path/line translation and payload-shape mapping: file_url, url_to_path, parse_paused, is_entry_break, render_value

cases.notes: file_url backslash-normalizes to forward slashes and prefixes 'file:///' (no extra slash before the drive letter). url_to_path detects a drive letter (rest.as_bytes()[1] == b':') after stripping 'file:///' and converts every '/' back to '\\'.
A POSIX path already starts with '/', so file_url does not insert a second one. url_to_path's non-drive-letter branch re-adds the leading '/' that stripping 'file:///' consumed.

Doesn't start with 'file:///', so the None branch returns the input unchanged — this is how a paused frame inside Node's own runtime internals gets a file value the UI can display (but not open in the editor).

CDP said lineNumber 4 (0-based); the app-facing StackFrame.line is 5 (1-based) — the +1 happens once, here, and nowhere else. scope_id prefers the first scope whose type is 'local' over the 'global' scope that precedes it in the chain.

An empty functionName is treated the same as a missing one and falls back to the literal string '(anonymous)'. An empty url with no scriptId->url entry in scripts resolves to the empty string, which url_to_path passes through unchanged since it doesn't start with 'file:///'.

Only the FIRST pause of a session can be the --inspect-brk entry halt, and only when its reason is exactly 'Break on start' (current V8) or 'other' (older Node) AND it hit no configured breakpoint. Case 2 shows the same params are no longer recognized once is_first is false (a later coincidental 'Break on start'/'other' with no hits, though unlikely in practice, would NOT be swallowed). Case 4 shows a real breakpoint hit on the very first pause is never mistaken for the entry break even though it is technically the first pause. Case 5 has no hitBreakpoints field at all — missing is treated as empty (unwrap_or(true)) — but it's still rejected because 'exception' isn't one of the two recognized reasons.
Strings are wrapped in literal double quotes for display; the quoting is added by render_value, not present in CDP's own value field.
Falls through to the default branch: the raw CDP 'value' field, JSON-stringified.
Literal string, independent of any 'value'/'description' field being present.
Objects render as their CDP 'description' (falling back to the literal 'Object' if description is absent, not exercised by this vector); objectId is carried straight through as the expandable marker.
